# Release checklist

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

This checklist applies to the next functional-preview release. Do not use
“research-validated” until every research gate in [STATUS.md](STATUS.md) is complete.

## Source and identity

- [x] Baseline release is committed and annotated as `v0.1.0`.
- [x] Product name is **ModDotPlot Browser**; technical packages and archives retain
  `moddotplot-interactive`; license is MIT-0 in the root and packaged crates.
- [x] Canonical authorship is in [PROVENANCE.md](PROVENANCE.md); generated prose uses
  the standard file note.
- [x] `CITATION.cff` requests the original ModDotPlot citation and credits method and
  historical reference implementations.
- [x] Release scope is local-only. No deployment, upload, hosted URL, or external
  publication is part of this cycle.

## Scientific gate

- [x] Production configuration is immutable, validated, versioned, and digestible.
- [x] Exact distinct canonical k-mers are the independent containment oracle.
- [x] The browser-default preview, detailed, and selective-composite production paths
  have assertion-backed exact-containment acceptance tests.
- [x] Verified-winner OPH and HLL p10 are supported by the documented sweep.
- [x] Initial terminal views enter exact mode before their first tile.
- [x] `U/u` normalization and coordinate behavior are documented and tested.
- [x] Rejected estimator and fused-projection executable paths have been removed from
  default artifacts or isolated in validation-only code.
- [x] Freeze the new release config version/digests and record them in generated
  parameters and release notes.
- [x] Run the bounded release statistical report and attach its complete machine-readable
  output, command, hardware, commit, and pass/fail interpretation.

## Correctness and browser gate

Run from a clean checkout:

```sh
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features validation -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --features validation
cargo check -p moddotplot-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown
npm --prefix web ci
npm --prefix web run verify
```

- [x] Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit integration covers rapid replacement load, clear,
  exact entry, unexpected egress, keyboard navigation, and context restoration.
- [x] The same suite passes in installed Google Chrome; WebKit 26.5 provides automated
  Safari-engine coverage. Actual Safari WebDriver requires the user's disabled global
  “Allow remote automation” setting and was not enabled by the release process.
- [x] Inject worker crash and prepared-axis allocation rejection and verify useful
  recovery paths.
- [x] Confirm self/pairwise plots, forward/reverse mode, reset, rapid zoom, cache
  eviction policy, resize, gzip, ambiguity, and short inputs.

## Performance and resource gate

- [x] Frozen axes and pre-allocation admission bound the main Wasm structures.
- [x] Tile/axis caches are byte bounded and use coordinated eviction.
- [x] Fused projection was benchmarked and rejected for first-paint latency.
- [x] Record current time to first coherent structure, stable viewport, Wasm/JS/GPU
  memory, and cancellation latency for representative self and pairwise chromosomes.
- [x] Confirm no monotonic live-cache growth during a fixed pan/zoom trace.
- [x] Clearly retain the 1 Gb input value as an upper bound rather than a laptop
  performance guarantee until sharding/spill validation is complete.
- [x] Run the generated million-record annotation parser/publication gate and enforce
  explicit per-file byte and matching-record admission limits.

## Reproducibility and distribution gate

- [x] Rust, Node/npm, dependencies, and CI actions are pinned.
- [x] One `npm --prefix web run build` command generates and tests the static release.
- [x] `SBOM.cdx.json` and `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt` are generated from locked packages
  plus checked-in license assets for embedded third-party data such as ColorBrewer and
  d3-scale-chromatic Viridis.
- [ ] Generate separate source and binary archives in a local packaging preflight;
  regenerate them from the annotated release commit as the final step.
- [ ] Attach SHA-256 checksums and build provenance: commit, dirty-state check, OS,
  architecture, Rust, wasm-pack, wasm-bindgen/wasm-opt, Node, and npm versions.
- [ ] Rebuild twice from clean checkouts; confirm byte identity or document the exact
  nondeterministic fields.
- [ ] Verify the binary archive contains `LICENSE`, notices, license bundle, SBOM,
  citation metadata, user guide, and deployable static assets.

## Privacy and local-static-artifact gate

- [x] Source and automated fixture processing show no application data egress.
- [x] A restrictive CSP is present in the static document.
- [x] Keep the restrictive document CSP in the static archive. HTTP response headers
  remain the responsibility of any future host and are not claimed by this local build.
- [x] Confirm no analytics, CDN, source maps, or unexpected external URLs are present
  in the production artifact. Development-only loopback WebSocket permissions are
  explicit in the document CSP.
- [x] Document that `file://` is unsupported and HTTP/HTTPS serving is required.

## Local release finalization

- [x] Update versions consistently in Cargo, npm, CFF, provenance, UI, changelog, and
  release notes.
- [ ] Commit generated SBOM/licenses and release evidence.
- [ ] Create and verify an annotated tag from a clean tree as the final source action.
- [ ] Produce source/binary archives, checksums, provenance, release notes, and known
  limitations under the local ignored `release-artifacts/` directory.
- [x] Do not push, publish, deploy, or upload any release material.
